title.narrative: Fas III - Lokala fredsdialoger genom ILC i DRK 2022-2025
Phase III - Local peace dialogues by ILC in DRC 2022-2025

description.narrative: 1. Stärka, och så småningom börja replikera i Nordkivu och/eller i Ituri, den "Murhesadynamik" som inleddes 2019 och som syftar till att öppna ett fönster av förtroende bland lokala ledare över de etniska/samhälleliga gränserna. Förväntade resultat: ökad samstämmighet och sammanhållning mellan fredsskapande processer (Nairobi, Luanda, Murhesa, P-DDRCS, SSR och Demokratiska Republiken Kongos åtaganden i Addis Abeba 2013); 2. Nationell retreat och uppföljningsworkshop om kongolesisk sammanhållning vid kriser (särskilt i Nordkivu): Förväntade resultat: Ökad urskiljning mellan externa och interna faktorer som förklarar Demokratiska Republiken Kongos utmanande mänskliga indikatorer och dess återkommande cykler av extremt våld och polarisering, vilket leder till modiga åtaganden, korrigering av gamla missuppfattningar och sunda och sammanhållna rekommendationer till det högsta ledarskapet.
Insatsen syftar till att stödja Initiative for Cohesive Leadership (ILC) i deras arbete med att skapa förutsättningar för fredsdialog och konfliktlösning/medling.
The initiative aims to support Initiative for Cohesive Leadership (ILC) in their work to create conditions for peace dialogue and conflict resolution / mediation.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
During the first ten months of the project's implementation, there were some delays, largely due to the election period and the complex process of establishing the new government at both the national and provincial levels. While it may be argued that the prior work of ILC and its partners contributed to mitigating major violence during the election period, it is difficult to directly attribute this outcome to ILC's efforts alone. Measuring the impact of violence prevention is inherently challenging, and establishing a direct cause-and-effect relationship remains near impossible.
Importantly, ILC has managed to build a quality interaction with the Vice-Premature in charge of Home affairs and the executive levels of intelligence services (ANR): presence of high cadres at the ILC-ADCI-DDRCS Uvira retreat with 30 warlords of "South South-Kivu", mutual understanding on the apolitical nature of ILC and ADCIs work (which entails that in no way will ILC move away from what is perceived by retreat participants as common goals and the greater good.
The added value of this contribution lies in the innovative methodology employed during retreats for community leaders linked to armed groups. These retreats focused on concrete, actionable steps to prevent armed conflict, rather than simply offering recommendations. Additionally, the ILC provided valuable contextual analysis, shedding light on the dynamics of the armed groups and their regional dimensions.
The approach of bringing together leaders from different armed groups for a collective dialogue on shared responsibility is unique and proactive. It is a community-centered strategy that appears to be highly effective in this context, where there is a pressing need for healing and the development of empowered, gender-responsive leaders.
Based on the fragile yet precious and promising collaboration initiated with the new leadership since June 2024, and strengthened by successful joint efforts for a ceasefire in Kwamouth territory in September and October, ILC engaged key actors from the Ministry of Interior (vice-Prime Minister, Secretary generals for Affaires coutumieres and Interior, Security), local State actors and non-State actors identified by ILC and other conflict resolution organisations on ways of addressing violent crises in a collegial, complementary fashion. A cease-fire agreement was signed in Mai-Ndombe which is a major achievement but the cease-fire is still fragile and more work need to be invested to ensure lasting peace.
One specific concept that was effectively implemented is the 'cadres consultatifs provinciaux', which serves as a tool to foster enhanced dialogue between central and local state actors, as well as non-state actors, on local issues. When necessary, it also facilitates decentralized communication flows for early warning, anticipation, prevention, and joint crisis response. This method has proven to be successful and is now being further developed to improve its effectiveness and long lasting outcomes.
